sections.name: Diablos gang
sections.card:
Summary: A small Latin American gang that holds the Hepburn Heights district of Portland and is not well armed.
Weak points: They are lightly armed: baseball bats only, except in missions, where they also carry guns.
Looks like: Two outfits: red bandana, dark blue jacket and light blue jeans; or blue bandana, olive cargo pants and the same jacket.
Tips: Diablo Stallions are their cars in every game they appear in. The Uptown Yardies are their arch rivals.

sections.name: Triad gang
sections.card:
Summary: A Chinese criminal gang that holds Chinatown plus the Callahan Point area of Portland.
Looks like: Members dress in blue boiler suits with black bandannas.
Tips: Expect baseball bats or pistols from members. The Leone Family are their enemies, and the rivalry is fierce.

sections.name: Leone Family (the Mafia)
sections.card:
Summary: An Italian mafia family based mainly in Saint Mark's, Portland, with a stake in Trenton, Chinatown and the Red Light District; the wiki names it the most dangerous gang, thanks to its shotguns.
Looks like: Their men dress in black suits and some add sunglasses; the gang car is the Mafia Sentinel, which is gray in the original game.
Tips: Their shotguns can blow up an ordinary car in two shots, so a vehicle within their range does not last long. They are fierce rivals of the Triads.

sections.name: Colombian Cartel
sections.card:
Summary: A drug cartel from Colombia that seized control of some of Shoreside Vale and Staunton Island and is deeply tied to the drug trade.
Looks like: Members dress in Hawaiian shirts and combat pants, with cowboy boots and Akruba-style hats, in the original game.
Tips: The Yakuza and the Leone Family are its biggest enemies. In the original game the gang drives the Cartel Cruiser.

sections.name: Uptown Yardies
sections.card:
Summary: A mostly Jamaican gang from Staunton Island; these days you only find them in Newport, though they also seem to deal near Liberty Campus.
Looks like: Members wear a short-sleeved black hoodie with a tan vest, tan pants and brown shoes, and the gang's two member models look alike.
Tips: Members carry baseball bats; the wiki also lists a pistol and, in some missions, an Uzi. Their Yardie Lobo lowriders are the only cars here with hydraulic suspension, and the Diablos are their rivals.

sections.name: Military (the Army)
sections.card:
Summary: The Army starts chasing you when your wanted level hits six stars, a step after the FBI at five stars, and the Rhino tank appears at that level too.
Weak points: A Rhino is nearly immune to small-arms fire. Explosives and flame weapons (molotovs, the flamethrower) hurt it. The windshield is its only soft spot, and you only see that when you go up against a military Rhino to hijack it.
Tips: In the original game, soldiers drop grenades when you kill them. The authorities seldom fire the cannon of the Rhino.

sections.name: Body armor
sections.card:
Summary: Armor is a second layer of protection on top of your health, taking hits from gunfire, blasts and flames. In the original game it shows up as a shield icon and gives nearly as many hit points as full health.
Uses: In Grand Theft Auto III, it also soaks up damage from falls, vehicle hits while you are on foot, and melee blows too.
Tips: In the original game, it costs $3,000 at Ammu-Nation after you finish Last Requests, and getting into a Police or SWAT Enforcer truck also gives you some. Collecting 50 hidden packages puts a permanent armor pickup outside every safehouse.

sections.name: Health pickups
sections.card:
Summary: A pickup that fills your health to the maximum; in Grand Theft Auto III they are found in front of every hospital and spread around Liberty City, often in places like shopping centers, parks and rest stops.
Uses: Health is shown as a number that starts out capped at 100%, and paying a prostitute can push it as high as 125%.
Tips: When your health hits zero you are wasted: you end up at the nearest hospital, pay a fee, lose every weapon and fail any mission you were on. In the original game, saving at a save point does not restore health, unlike every other 3D Universe game except Advance.

sections.name: Adrenaline pills
sections.card:
Summary: Pills lying around Liberty City that give a short burst of speed while time seems to slow down.
Uses: Your aim keeps its normal speed while everything else slows, which is handy against police and gangs, and you also jump further than usual.
Tips: Getting into a vehicle ends the speed boost. One lies in Trenton behind the big sign on the roof of Liberty Pharmaceuticals.

sections.name: Police bribe
sections.card:
Summary: In Grand Theft Auto III each police bribe is a spinning police badge shaped like a star; picking it up drops your wanted level one star. The wiki calls it a free alternative to getting your car resprayed.
Uses: In Grand Theft Auto III, a bribe does not stop the stronger forces already after you, such as the Army, SWAT or the FBI, though no more of their vehicles turn up. A Police Maverick is the one exception: at three stars it breaks off, and you drop to two.
Tips: Bribes are rare, so learn where they are: a few are in plain sight and others are tucked out of view. In Grand Theft Auto III, some can only be reached by jumping a vehicle.

sections.name: Hidden packages
sections.card:
Summary: Liberty City hides 100 packages, each a white bale tied up with brown adhesive tape that pays $1,000; every tenth one unlocks a lasting item pickup outside the safehouses.
Uses: In the original game a pager message announces each reward, and a pickup for that item then waits permanently outside every safehouse: 10 pistol, 20 Uzi, 30 grenades, 40 shotgun, 50 body armor, 60 molotov cocktails, 70 AK47, 80 sniper rifle, 90 M16, and at 100 the rocket launcher plus $1,000,000.
Tips: Pick them up on foot; driving over one does not count. You need all of them for 100% completion.

sections.name: Rocket launcher
sections.card:
Summary: A one-shot rocket launcher that can wreck almost any vehicle or pedestrian; in the original game you can buy it for $25,000 at Phil Cassidy's Army Surplus in Rockford, Staunton Island, once you have finished Arms Shortage.
Uses: Its weight holds you to a jog and rules out jumping while it is in your hands. Rockets go exactly where you aim, and it can bring down police helicopters that chase you, but it will not finish off a tank such as the Rhino in one hit.
Tips: Gather every one of the 100 hidden packages and one appears at every safehouse. Another is in Cedar Grove, at the western end of The Homes (the stretch nearest Cochrane Dam): the big pink house there has one on its roof, along the western side.

sections.name: AK47 assault rifle
sections.card:
Summary: In the original game the AK47 trades damage for speed: it fires very fast but hits weakly. Ammu-Nation in Newport sells it for $3,000 after you finish Last Requests.
Uses: In the original game you cannot aim it in first person, unlike the M16. Its recoil is gentler, but the M16 beats it otherwise: it does far more damage, fires faster and holds twice as many rounds.
Tips: Collecting 70 hidden packages puts one at each safehouse. There is also one in Trenton, behind the big sign on the roof of Liberty Pharmaceuticals, beside adrenaline, health and armor pickups; reach it by jumping from the elevated tracks.

sections.name: Molotov cocktails
sections.card:
Summary: A thrown bottle that can light up vehicles and any cluster of pedestrians; using one usually brings a wanted level of up to three stars.
Uses: Anyone on foot who stands close to the flames burns to death. Molotovs are one of the flame weapons that can hurt a Rhino.
Tips: In the other 3D games a molotov or two will down a police helicopter, but not in Grand Theft Auto III. In Grand Theft Auto III, collecting 60 hidden packages puts one at every safehouse, and the pickup on the upper level of Liberty Campus's courtyard gives 10.

sections.name: Rhino tank
sections.card:
Summary: A heavy armored tank with a cannon that turns up once your wanted level reaches six stars; it runs on wheels rather than tracks.
Uses: Small arms fire and crashes do almost nothing to it, and any vehicle it hits blows up or catches fire, which is handy against wanted levels because police cars tend to ram you. Its cannon is devastating to most vehicles.
Looks like: Boxy and truck-like, with three axles, a slim windshield, big doors along both sides and a turret on its roof; it only comes in a faded green.
Tips: It handles poorly: even at low speed it turns in a wide circle, and it accelerates very slowly. Its side doors also leave you open to being busted or dragged out by a hostile pedestrian. You can get one at Portland Harbor after you have collected every emergency vehicle for Import/Export.
